text.p: British retailer Storehouse Plc on Thursday reported a nine percent rise in profits for the last year and said it would create 1,000 jobs over three years in a 120 million pounds ($197.4 million) expansion and modernisation programme.

The retailer, whose outlets are Bhs and children's wear chain Mothercare, said profits before tax and exceptional charges rose to 118.3 million pounds, from 108.7 million in the previous year. Sales were up 15.3 percent to 1.25 billion.
The group said in the eight weeks to May 17, including Easter, total sales were 15.5 percent ahead of the same period a year ago.
Sales at Bhs were up by 6.7 percent and Mothercare sales, excluing Childrens World bought from Boots Co Plc last year, rose by 5.7 percent.
Chief executive Keith Edelman said the company had had a satisfactory year, but Mothercare's performance was disappointing.
"Mothercare, operating in a highly competitive children's wear market, was below expectations."
Edelman said the 120 million pound ($197.4 million) investment would be spent on new stores, redesigning Bhs and the conversion on Childrens World to Mothercare World. ($ = 0.607 British Pounds)
